source_read: Publisher HTML (JAMA Network, doi:10.1001/jama.2015.6358), full text shown without sign-in. First attempt showed a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' check page, which was not touched; one retry several minutes later loaded the article, read with get_page_text (abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions, article information including the correction footnote, reference list). Tables 1 to 3 read from the page's text copies; Table 2 also viewed as its 'View Large' image, including the footnotes; Figures 2, 3 and 4 (forest plots) viewed as their 'View Large' images on screen (not downloaded). Figure 1 (flow diagram) not viewed. A later revisit to check the heading tree showed the check page again and was abandoned. Online supplements (eAppendices 1 to 13) not read; the four separate correction notices not opened (the article's own correction footnote was read). Text and image notes saved in scratchpad/can-a/s219/whiting_2015_jama_text.txt.

claims.overstatement: None. The claim keeps the source's association wording, gives the review team's low GRADE rating, and says the active-comparator trials were not pooled. One small misplacement of a number: the source's '15 studies' with prochlorperazine counts every trial with a prochlorperazine arm, including 2 three-arm THC trials that also had placebo (Table 1), so prochlorperazine was the comparator in 13 of the 20 active-only trials, not 15. The claim could add that the review says, without pooling, that all trials favoured cannabinoids over both active comparators and placebo, not significantly in all.
claims.note: Numbers re-found: 28 studies, 1772 participants; nabilone 14, THC 6, levonantradol 4, dronabinol 3, nabiximols 1; risk of bias high 23, unclear 5; 8 placebo-controlled (3 of them also with an active arm), 20 active only; pooled complete response OR 3.82 (1.55 to 9.42), 3 parallel-group trials, 102 patients, dronabinol 2 and nabiximols 1, I2 0%, GRADE low. Editors' arithmetic 47 - 20 = 27 per 100: same. The 47% and 20% appear only in the abstract and the article has no forest plot for this outcome, so their derivation cannot be checked; for pain the abstract's percentages equal summed events over summed patients in Figure 2, so these are probably crude summed proportions too. As a check, an OR of 3.82 applied to a 20% placebo rate implies about 49%, consistent with 47%.

anchors.locator: Results › Nausea and Vomiting Due to Chemotherapy, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: 28 studies (37 reports; 1772 participants): nabilone 14, dronabinol 3, nabiximols 1, levonantradol 4, THC 6; 2 also had a dronabinol plus ondansetron or prochlorperazine arm. 8 placebo-controlled (3 of these also with an active comparator); 20 active comparator only; commonest comparators prochlorperazine (15), chlorpromazine (2), domperidone (2). Risk of bias high in 23, unclear in 5. All studies favoured cannabinoids over active comparators and placebo, not significantly in all. Complete response more frequent with dronabinol or nabiximols than placebo, OR 3.82 (95% CI 1.55 to 9.42), 3 trials, I2 0%, similar for both drugs.

claims.overstatement: None of substance; the claim is more cautious than the source, whose Results text calls the 30% responder result and the Brief Pain Inventory result greater reductions although both intervals include no difference. Minor points: 'adults' is not stated in the main text; 'mostly nabiximols' holds for the pooled analyses (7 of 8 and 6 of 6 trials) but nabiximols was 13 of the 28 trials, the largest single group, not most of them.
claims.note: Every number re-found in Results › Chronic Pain, Table 2 and Figure 2. The abstract's 37% and 31% are the crude summed proportions of Figure 2's overall row: 254/685 = 37.1% and 215/685 = 31.4%, a difference of 5.7 per 100 (editors' 'about 6 more in 100': same); 685 + 685 = 1370 patients, as in Table 2. So the derivation, though not described in words, can be reconstructed from Figure 2. Moderate-rated outcomes: 30% responders OR 1.41 (0.99 to 2.00), NRS -0.46 (-0.80 to -0.11), BPI -0.17 (-0.50 to 0.16), Neuropathic Pain Scale -3.89 (-7.32 to -0.47) on 0 to 100, EQ-5D -0.01 (-0.05 to 0.02): the claim's 'not statistically significant or small' is accurate. No minimal clinically important difference is named in the main text (the protocol is in a supplement not read). The nabiximols-only subtotal for 30% responders is OR 1.32 (0.94 to 1.86), 7 trials (Figure 2), not in the claim.

anchors.locator: Results › Chronic Pain, 3rd paragraph
anchors.extracted: The text gives the cancer-pain subgroup (2 trials) exactly the overall estimate, OR 1.41 (0.99 to 2.00), which is probably a copying error (from Figure 2, the two cancer-pain trials give OR 2.81 and 0.90), and reports the BPI result as a greater reduction although its interval includes zero.

claims.overstatement: No overstatement of benefit; three errors of detail. (1) Barthel index: -0.58 (-1.73 to 0.56) is not a 4-trial estimate. Table 2 prints three unlabelled estimates in that cell beside the labels Nabilone (2), Dronabinol (1), THC/CBD (1): -0.58 (-1.73 to 0.56), 0.23 (-0.13 to 0.59) and -0.03 (-0.39 to 0.33). Figure 3 shows that this layout gives one estimate per cannabinoid, not an overall (see (2)), so -0.58 is the nabilone estimate from 2 trials. A pool of all four could not have an interval of plus or minus 1.15 when two of its parts have intervals of plus or minus 0.36. The review gives no overall Barthel estimate. All three intervals include zero, so 'did not change' stands. (2) The magnitude's 'Table 2 still prints -0.11, -0.23 to 0.02' presents that figure as an uncorrected overall. Figure 3 shows -0.11 (-0.23 to 0.02) is the nabiximols subtotal (4 trials, 383 vs 337 patients), printed beside the label Nabiximols (4). The other two Table 2 values are the dronabinol (-0.94) and THC/CBD (-0.32) arms of Zajicek 2003. The corrected overall, -0.12 (-0.24 to 0.01), is in the abstract, the Results text and Figure 3. (3) 'The outcome rated moderate (Ashworth)': the review rated three spasticity outcomes moderate (Ashworth, Barthel index, walking speed), and none showed a clear difference, which strengthens the claim's point. Smaller points: 'on 0 to 10 scales' for patient-rated spasticity is not stated for that pool (Table 2 says NRS or VAS scores; the text says numerical rating scales). '1,244 people' matches Table 2, but Figure 3's overall row counts 590 + 544 = 1,134. 'Mostly nabiximols' is 6 of 14 trials. Follow-up is printed only for some spasticity outcomes (3 to 15 weeks).
claims.note: Re-found: 14 studies (2280), MS 11 (2138), paraplegia 3 (142), only MS studies pooled; risk of bias low 2, unclear 5, high 7. Patient-rated spasticity -0.76 (-1.38 to -0.14), 3 trials (698), I2 73, low; global impression OR 1.44 (1.07 to 1.94), 3 (461), low; Ashworth overall -0.12 (-0.24 to 0.01), 5 trials, I2 0, moderate, corrected online July 13 2015 per the article's correction footnote; 50% reduction OR 1.40 (0.81 to 2.41) and 30% reduction OR 1.64 (0.95 to 2.83), 2 trials (519) each, low; walking speed -0.86 (-3.08 to 1.36), 2 (497), moderate. Figure 3 also shows Zajicek 2003 entering the overall Ashworth pool twice (dronabinol and THC/CBD arms against the same 207 placebo patients; combined weight 1.7%), against the review's stated rule of one data set per study; the effect on the estimate is negligible (-0.11 to -0.12).

claims.overstatement: None; the claim is more cautious than the review, whose conclusions call the evidence low quality but suggestive of improvement for HIV weight gain, sleep disorders and Tourette syndrome, and speak of 'no effect' on psychosis and depression where the claim correctly says the intervals are too wide. The framing 'too few, small or short to show whether they help' is the editors' summary; it agrees with the review's own call for larger trials in exactly these conditions and its remark that the small trials may have lacked power.
claims.note: All numbers re-found. Sleep-apnoea trial: the review and Table 2 attribute it to nabilone, but the only sleep-apnoea report in the reference list is ref 18 (Prasad et al., 2011, a conference abstract of a dronabinol trial). The 2 sleep studies' 5 reports are ref 18 plus the four reports of the fibromyalgia nabilone-amitriptyline trial (refs 63, 64, 89, 90), and Table 1 lists sleep among the indications of dronabinol against placebo; the claim's parenthesis is supported. Table 2 gives the sleep-quality pool as 8 trials (539 patients) and the sleep-disturbance pool as 3 trials (1637 patients); the two patient counts look transposed or otherwise wrong, and neither is in the claim. The depression rows in Table 2 (HADS 0.15, MADRS 1.90, BDI 0.69, single trials) and the text's highest-dose result (2.50, 0.38 to 4.62) are as the claim gives them.

anchors.locator: Results › Sleep Disorder, 1st paragraph; Table 2, Sleep disorder rows; References 18, 63, 64, 89, 90; Table 1, dronabinol and nabilone rows
anchors.extracted: 2 studies (5 reports; 54 participants) of sleep problems: a parallel trial at high risk of bias, apnoea-hypopnoea index -19.64 (P = .02), 22 patients, 3 weeks, attributed to nabilone, GRADE low; and a crossover trial at low risk of bias in fibromyalgia, nabilone vs amitriptyline, insomnia -3.25 (-5.26 to -1.24), restfulness 0.48 (0.01 to 0.95). 19 placebo-controlled trials for pain or MS (13 nabiximols) measured sleep: sleep quality -0.58 (-0.87 to -0.29), 8 trials; sleep disturbance -0.26 (-0.52 to 0.00), 3 trials; both very low. Ref 18 is a dronabinol sleep-apnoea abstract.

anchors.locator: Results › Appetite Stimulation in HIV/AIDS Infection, 1st paragraph; Table 2, HIV/AIDS row
anchors.extracted: 4 studies (255 participants), all dronabinol, 3 against placebo (one also with smoked cannabis) and 1 against megestrol acetate; all at high risk of bias. Weight gain of 2 kg or more within 6 weeks: OR 2.2 (0.68 to 7.27), 1 trial, 88 patients, low. The cannabis-and-dronabinol trial found significantly more weight gain than placebo; megestrol acetate gave more weight gain than dronabinol.

anchors.locator: Results › Anxiety Disorder, 1st paragraph; Table 2, Anxiety disorder row
anchors.extracted: One small parallel trial at high risk of bias in generalized social anxiety disorder: cannabidiol vs placebo, anxiety factor of a visual analogue mood scale -16.52 (P = .01) during a simulated public-speaking test; 24 patients, follow-up 107 minutes, very low.

anchors.locator: Results › Depression, 1st paragraph; Table 2, Depression rows
anchors.extracted: No trials of cannabinoids for depression; 5 trials for other conditions (4 pain, 1 MS) reported depression; 3 found no difference; one graded-dose nabiximols trial found worse scores at the highest dose (2.50, 0.38 to 4.62) and none at the two lower doses. Table 2 single trials: HADS 0.15 (-1.0 to 1.31), MADRS 1.90 (-0.22 to 4.02), BDI 0.69 (-0.76 to 2.14), all very low.

anchors.locator: Results › Psychosis; Results › Glaucoma; Results › Movement Disorders Due to Tourette Syndrome; Table 2, Psychosis and Tourette syndrome rows
anchors.extracted: Psychosis: 2 studies (71 participants), high risk of bias, cannabidiol vs amisulpride or placebo, no difference; BPRS -0.10 (-9.20 to 8.90) and PANSS 1 (-12.60 to 14.60), 35 patients, low. Glaucoma: one crossover trial of 6, unclear risk of bias, no difference in intraocular pressure. Tourette: 2 placebo-controlled trials (36 participants) of THC capsules; single-trial differences on four tic scales with 17 or 18 patients (P = .03, < .05, .061, .008), low.

anchors.locator: Discussion › Strengths and Weaknesses, 1st paragraph; Discussion › Unanswered Questions and Future Research
anchors.extracted: Very small samples (glaucoma 6, Tourette mean 18, sleep disorder mean 27, anxiety 24) may have lacked power; larger robust trials are needed for HIV weight gain, depression, sleep disorders, anxiety, psychosis, glaucoma and Tourette syndrome.

anchors.locator: Abstract › Conclusions and Relevance; Discussion, 2nd paragraph; Methods › Study Eligibility Criteria
anchors.extracted: Review's conclusions: low-quality evidence suggesting improvement in HIV weight gain, sleep disorders and Tourette syndrome; very low for anxiety; low-quality evidence of no effect on psychosis and very low of no effect on depression. The prespecified indications do not include epilepsy.

claims.overstatement: 'Increase' is acceptable for randomized comparisons, and the claim names the highest-dose choice and the short-term limit. One sentence goes too far: 'The review reports odds ratios only, not how many people in 100 had each effect' holds for Table 3, but for 'any adverse event' Figure 4 prints event counts for every study and in total (1438/1779 with cannabinoids vs 1058/1710 with comparators, crude 81% vs 62%, editors' arithmetic). Suggested: 'apart from the counts for any adverse event in a forest plot, the review reports odds ratios only'. Also note that the comparators in the AE pools include active drugs: Figure 4's 'placebo' column includes active-comparator trials, as Table 3's title says.
claims.note: All odds ratios, intervals, study and patient counts re-found in Table 3; I2 31% (any), 0% (serious), 2% (withdrawal). AE data in 62 studies (127 reports). Meta-regression and stratified analyses found no difference in the any-AE association by cannabinoid, design, indication, comparator or follow-up. Figure 4 has 29 studies but 1779 + 1710 = 3489 patients, against 3714 in Table 3, an unexplained discrepancy. The review gives no GRADE rating for adverse events (Table 2 covers benefit outcomes only); the claim's 'moderate' is the editors' own rating.

anchors.locator: Results › Adverse Events, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: AE data in 62 studies (127 reports). No evidence that the any-AE association differed by cannabinoid, design, indication, comparator or follow-up duration, so all studies were combined. Cannabinoids associated with much greater risk of any AE, serious AE, withdrawal due to AE and several specific AEs. No studies of long-term AEs found, even when searching lower levels of evidence.

key_findings.note: Nabilone against active drugs: dihydrocodeine 1, amitriptyline 1, chlorpromazine 1, alizapride 1, domperidone 2, prochlorperazine 7 = 13; cannabidiol 4 (capsules 2 against placebo, 1 against amisulpride, spray 1).

key_findings.correction: '20 against an active drug only, most often prochlorperazine (15 studies)': the source's 15 counts every trial with a prochlorperazine arm among the 23 with an active comparator; Table 1 shows 2 of them (THC against placebo and prochlorperazine) also had a placebo arm, so prochlorperazine was the comparator in 13 of the 20 active-only trials. Suggested: 'prochlorperazine was the comparator in 15 trials (13 of the 20 active-only trials and 2 three-arm trials with placebo)'. The same misplacement is in the claim cl_can_med_chemo_nausea.

key_findings.note: Figure 2 (viewed by this reader as its View Large image) gives the counts: overall 254/685 vs 215/685, so the abstract's 37% vs 31% are crude summed proportions (37.1% vs 31.4%). The note's 'how those percentages were derived is not described' is true of the text, but the derivation can be reconstructed. Reader's DerSimonian-Laird recomputation from the printed counts reproduces OR 1.41 (0.99 to 2.00), the nabiximols subtotal 1.32 (0.94 to 1.86) and the neuropathic (non-cancer) subgroup 1.38 (0.93 to 2.03) exactly.

key_findings.correction: (a) 'Barthel ADL -0.58 (-1.73 to 0.56), 4 trials': in Table 2 that cell holds three unlabelled estimates beside Nabilone (2), Dronabinol (1), THC/CBD (1): -0.58 (-1.73 to 0.56), 0.23 (-0.13 to 0.59), -0.03 (-0.39 to 0.33). Figure 3 shows the same layout in the Ashworth row gives one estimate per product. -0.58, with a standard error of about 0.58, cannot be a pool that includes estimates with standard errors of about 0.18. So -0.58 is the nabilone estimate (2 trials), and no 4-trial Barthel estimate is reported. All three intervals include zero. (b) The note 'Table 2 still prints -0.11 (-0.23 to 0.02)': Figure 3 shows -0.11 (-0.23 to 0.02) is the nabiximols subtotal (Collin 2010, Collin 2007, Wade 2004, Berman 2007; 383 vs 337 patients), not an uncorrected overall. The other two Table 2 values are the dronabinol (-0.94, -2.37 to 0.49) and THC/CBD (-0.32, -1.59 to 0.95) arms of Zajicek 2003. The overall -0.12 (-0.24 to 0.01) is printed in Figure 3 as well as in the abstract and text. (c) '1244 patients' is Table 2's figure; Figure 3's overall row gives 590 + 544 = 1134.

key_findings.note: The note's account of the April 2016 correction (wording of the insomnia and restfulness estimates) was not checked by this reader: the separate correction notices were not opened, and the article's own correction footnote says only that it was for an incorrect effect estimate.

The methods are described correctly as stated. Figure 3 shows one departure from the one-data-set-per-trial rule: Zajicek 2003 enters the overall Ashworth pool twice (dronabinol and THC/CBD arms against the same 207 placebo patients; weights 0.75% and 0.95%). With either arm alone the overall is -0.11 (reader's recomputation), so the effect is negligible.

reporting_issues.note: Figure 3 resolves the unlabelled cells. In the Ashworth row they are per-product estimates in the order of the cannabinoid column: nabiximols subtotal of 4 trials -0.11 (-0.23 to 0.02), THC/CBD -0.32 (-1.59 to 0.95) and dronabinol -0.94 (-2.37 to 0.49), the last two from the two arms of Zajicek 2003. Table 2 prints no overall; the corrected overall -0.12 (-0.24 to 0.01) is in Figure 3, the abstract and the text. So the issue is not that Table 2 kept an uncorrected overall: it never printed one. The Barthel row has the same layout, so its first value, -0.58 (-1.73 to 0.56), is the nabilone estimate (2 trials) and no 4-trial overall exists (see key finding 7). The table footnotes do exist, on the table image (View Large), but do not explain the cells. Consequence to add: -0.58 must not be cited as a pooled estimate of 4 trials; the card's key finding 7, its effect_sizes field and the claim cl_can_med_ms_spasticity all do so.

Reader's recomputation from Figure 2's counts for the two cancer-pain trials (Johnson 2010, 23/53 vs 12/56; Portenoy 2012, 22/90 vs 24/91), DerSimonian-Laird: OR 1.55 (0.51 to 4.70), I2 77% (editors' calculation). The printed 1.41 (0.99 to 2.00) is the overall estimate copied.
Found independently in step 1 (ref 18 dronabinol sleep-apnoea abstract; 5 reports = ref 18 + refs 63, 64, 89, 90; Table 1 lists sleep under dronabinol against placebo).
Recomputed: the printed interval implies a standard error of the log odds ratio of 0.039; with 470 patients the smallest possible is about 0.18.

The Ashworth part is explained by Figure 3: one three-arm trial (Zajicek 2003) enters as two comparisons, dronabinol and THC/CBD, sharing its placebo group, so there are 6 comparisons for 5 trials. The consequence should say this double-counts that placebo group, against the review's stated rule; the effect on the estimate is negligible. The chronic-pain (30 products for 28 studies) and Barthel (2 nabilone trials against 1 nabilone study in the Spasticity section) parts stand unexplained.

Literally correct for text and tables. For pain, Figure 2 shows the derivation: 254/685 = 37.1% and 215/685 = 31.4%, summed events over summed patients, i.e. crude pooled proportions, as the consequence assumes. The nausea percentages (47% vs 20%) cannot be traced, because the article has no forest plot for that outcome.

Table 2's footnotes exist on the table image (View Large): abbreviations (CBM = cannabis based medicine), a (no glaucoma studies in the estimate; THC and cannabidiol were the interventions), b (what the outcome cell contains; follow-up not shown for all studies), c (definitions of the four GRADE grades). They give no reasons for individual GRADE ratings, so the consequence holds for the whole article, not only for the HTML. The Supplement 1 versus Supplement 2 inconsistency is confirmed (Results, 1st and 3rd paragraphs).

risk_of_bias.note: AMSTAR 2 critically low (provisional) follows from items 7 and 15, as the card says. Item 11 'yes' is defensible, but Figure 3 shows a three-arm trial entered twice with a shared placebo group, against the stated rule (negligible weight); the any-AE pool also mixes placebo and active comparators under one 'placebo' column (Figure 4), which the card already notes from Table 3's title.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial. One qualification to point (5) and to the effect_sizes and selective_reporting fields: the summary gives no absolute numbers, but Figure 4 prints raw event counts for any adverse event (1438/1779 vs 1058/1710 across 29 studies; crude 81% vs 62%, editors' arithmetic), and Figure 2 prints the pain responder counts.

missed: Figures 2 to 4 (which the first reader could not load) were viewed by this reader as their View Large images. Figure 2's heterogeneity P values are misprinted: '.94' and '.64' should be .094 and .064 (recomputed from the printed counts; the I2 values 44.5% and 47.6% are right).
